title: Tacos al Pastor
subtitle: Marinated pork with pineapple on corn tortillas
excerpt: Tacos al pastor feature pork shoulder marinated in dried chillies, spices, and pineapple juice, then grilled or pan-roasted until deeply caramelised. The original is cooked on a vertical spit, but this home version achieves similar results by roasting thin slices in a very hot oven. Served on small corn tortillas with pineapple, onion, and coriander.
sourceNotes: Al pastor (in the style of the shepherd) was created by Lebanese immigrants in Mexico in the mid-20th century, adapting the shawarma spit technique to pork. The trompo (vertical spit) is the defining method for street vendors in Mexico City. The home adaptation roasts the marinated pork flat in a very hot oven to achieve the same caramelised crust.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked pork in portions. Defrost in the fridge overnight.
recipe.batchNotes: The marinade scales directly. Marinate a large batch and roast in portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight for the best flavour.
recipe.temperatureNote: fan oven — as hot as possible

content.text: Slice the pork thin (3 to 4 mm) before marinating. This increases the surface area for caramelisation and means each slice cooks quickly in a very hot oven. The marinade contains pineapple juice, which tenderises the meat through enzymatic action. Do not marinate for more than 12 hours or the pineapple will make the texture mushy.

items.prepNote: fresh or tinned, half in marinade, half diced for serving

white onion, finely diced, to serve
salsa roja or green salsa, to serve

content.text: Make the marinade: blend the rehydrated chillies with the garlic, half the pineapple, cumin, oregano, white wine vinegar, and 1 teaspoon of salt into a smooth paste. Add a little of the chilli soaking water if it won't blend.
Pour the marinade over the sliced pork. Mix to coat every slice. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

Heat the oven to its highest setting (240°C fan or higher). Spread the pork in a single layer on two baking trays. Roast for 12 to 15 minutes until the edges are dark and caramelised. Rest for 10 minutes, then chop roughly.
Serve the pork in warm small corn tortillas with diced pineapple, white onion, coriander, lime wedges, and salsa. The traditional way is two tortillas per taco, stacked.

items.symptom: Pork is steaming rather than caramelising in the oven
items.cause: Pork slices were stacked or the oven was not hot enough
items.fix: The pork must be in a single layer on the tray with some space between pieces. Use two trays and rotate them halfway through cooking. The oven must be fully preheated.
